neighbours.label: The word that raises an objection or snag after an all-is-well setup: ' why' in 'so why would/fix …?', ' only' / ' trouble' in 'the only problem/catch is', 'the trouble is'
fire: The shop is busy and the reviews are glowing, so why would the owner sell it now?
The car starts every morning and has never let us down, so why replace it?
The flat is bright and close to the station. The only problem is the rent.
The recipe is quick and the kids love it. The trouble is that it uses a whole block of butter.
Our tests pass and the users seem content, so why would anyone rewrite the module?
The hotel was spotless and the staff were kind; the only snag was the thin walls.
The plan is cheap and everyone has agreed to it. The trouble is that nobody has the time.
The garden is thriving and the neighbours admire it, so why tear it up?
quiet: The owner explained why the shop is busy on market days.
The mechanic showed us why the car starts slowly in winter.
The flat is bright and close to the station, and the rent is fair.
The recipe is quick, and it was the only dish the kids finished.
The report describes why the users prefer the older module.
The hotel was spotless, and ours was the only room with a balcony.
The plan is cheap and everyone has agreed to it, so we start on Monday.
The gardener asked why the neighbours had planted so many roses.

notes: Top tokens: ' only' x5, ' why' x5, ' problem' x3; output promotes ' instead', ' rather', ' why', ' failed', ' issue'. Probe: 'so why would we change anything?' 0.55, 'so why fix it?' 0.60, 'The trouble is' 0.47, 'the only catch' 0.33; plain 'explained why' 0.02, 'the only child' 0.01. Cleft 'it was only after … that' was weak (0.08), so the label is the objection, not the cleft.
